summary: Export verified native binary bundles for reuse

delivery.outcome: Export verified manifest-listed Python extensions, Rust cdylib and headers to a fresh standalone bundle through an API and CLI; test installed consumers and independently publish/merge.
nonGoals: Change counting, backend compilation, C ABI, dependencies or platform support.
Include optional Cargo rlib in wheel/export or promise atomic directory/crash-safe publication.
Publish to a registry, deploy, migrate consumers or edit protected policy.

architecture.decision: Reuse verify_artifacts for current or explicitly selected package. Snapshot and recheck all listed bytes before exclusive destination mkdir; reject duplicate/reserved export paths. Copy only artifacts/headers with exclusive file creation, preserving relative paths, and write manifest last. Existing destinations are never reused; interrupted copies may leave an incomplete owned output without a completed manifest. CLI delegates to the API and reports failures with nonzero status.
dataChanges: New standalone export directory reuses sorust.artifacts/v1 without schema changes.
architecture.rollback: Revert through independent protected review; preserve prior dist, test receipts and every generated worktree file.

validation.evidence: Installed API/CLI export exact listed bytes and manifest; independent Python/C clients execute exports; existing paths and invalid source inputs fail without overwriting data or creating output for invalid source.
Full build/runtime/C/Rust/Python and foreign/nested consumer export coverage passes.
Existing canonical v9 metadata/index/tracking verified, required remote checks and independent exact-head approval/merge; release own lease and preserve generated data before cleanup.
